reading.body:
Jason Smith's AI record holds 14 dated events: five recorded votes on bills and nine campaign contributions from Amazon and Google political committees.

The contributions cluster in two windows. Amazon PAC gave $3,000 in February 2025, $500 and $2,000 in July 2025, and $2,500 in May 2026. Google NetPAC gave $5,000 twice in February 2025 and $5,000 twice in March 2025, with two matching negative entries of $-5,000 on the same March date, which read as reversals or reclassifications of the earlier receipts rather than new money.

The votes are all yea. They fall on suspension motions, the procedure used for bills with broad support, in April, July, and January 2026, plus one in June 2026. The data does not name what any of the five bills would do, so it cannot show whether they touch data centers, grid interconnection, or procurement, which are the points where AI policy meets physical buildout.

What the record does not establish is causation or intent, and the page says so directly. Contributions and votes sit in date order because that is how they can be read together, not because one produced the other. The dollar amounts are small by federal standards and come from corporate PACs, not the companies themselves. A reader can see who gave and how he voted. A reader cannot see from this data alone whether the money and the votes are related, what the bills contained, or whether any of it bears on compute and power.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Jason Smith: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 14 events.
